# Straconis Software Dev Nexus Launcher 0.3.1-alpha

This release integrates launcher self-update with the 0.3.0 central catalog, branded desktop interface, and Windows installer.

## Downloads

- Windows per-user installer: `nexus-launcher-setup-0.3.1-alpha-windows-x86_64.exe`
- Windows portable ZIP: `nexus-launcher-windows-x86_64.zip`
- Linux x86_64: `nexus-launcher-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
- SHA-256 checksums: `SHA256SUMS.txt`

## Changes

- The LAUNCHER strip checks GitHub releases in the background and offers newer compatible versions. Alpha builds can see newer alphas; stable builds skip prereleases. Older versions are never offered.
- UPDATE LAUNCHER verifies a required SHA-256 checksum, extracts the official platform archive, and runs the new binary with `--check` before replacing the executable and restarting.
- Replacement preserves custom catalogs, central-service configuration, sign-in storage, and installed tools. A failed replacement restores the previous executable when possible. An unwritable installation directory stops the update without requesting elevation.
- Launcher update checks run in both standalone and central-service modes.
- Preserves 0.3.0 central administration, supported-project pages, status stamps, authenticated metadata caching, saved preferences, and Windows Start Menu integration.
- Includes the service-address preference, public-host deployment templates, and WordPress-native service/Hostinger bridge source added since the 0.3.0 release. The desktop installer does not install or deploy a broker or WordPress plugin.

## Installing this release

Published 0.1.0-alpha and 0.3.0-alpha builds do not contain the updater. Install 0.3.1-alpha manually once. Future releases can then be installed through UPDATE LAUNCHER. Managed applications still use REFRESH → UPDATE separately.

The Windows installer installs for the current user without administrator rights and creates Start → Straconis Software → Straconis Software Dev Nexus Launcher. Reinstall preserves edited catalogs; uninstall preserves catalog, configuration, and managed tool data. Windows binaries are unsigned. macOS binaries are not included.

Central administration needs a separately deployed service and its HTTPS address in Preferences. No server credentials or developer VM address are bundled. See `docs/central-admin.md` and `wordpress/README.md` in this tag for service setup.

This is an alpha release. Native credential prompts and the interactive updater still need hands-on verification on personal Windows systems.
